# Dev Ledger

> Dev Ledger is an open-source developer analytics application that turns GitHub history into a longitudinal record of source growth, activity patterns, languages, milestones, and project evolution.

Dev Ledger is available at https://devledger.site and its source is public at https://github.com/Aliferous3/dev-ledger. The hosted application authenticates through GitHub OAuth and a read-only GitHub App. Public product, legal, security, and blog pages may be indexed and summarized. Authenticated application routes, API endpoints, and telemetry relays are not intended for crawling.

Key data-handling facts: Dev Ledger does not persist repository source code, commit messages, pull-request titles, GitHub email addresses, GitHub OAuth access tokens, GitHub App installation tokens, or raw webhook payload bodies. It stores GitHub-derived metadata needed to compute analytics and maintain sync state.

## Product

- [Dev Ledger](https://devledger.site/): Live application and product entry point.
- [Security & Privacy](https://devledger.site/security): Public trust record covering access, storage, authentication, isolation, controls, and recovery.
- [Privacy Policy](https://devledger.site/privacy): Privacy policy for the hosted service.
- [Terms of Service](https://devledger.site/terms): Terms governing use of the hosted service.

## Blog

- [Dev Ledger Blog](https://devledger.site/blog): Writing about GitHub history, code metrics, developer analytics, privacy, and the systems behind Dev Ledger.
- [How to Analyze Your GitHub Development History](https://devledger.site/blog/analyze-github-development-history): A practical guide to reading source growth, churn, commits, active days, languages, and repository evolution.
- [GitHub Analytics: 12 Metrics Worth Tracking and What They Actually Mean](https://devledger.site/blog/github-analytics-metrics-guide): A practical guide to 12 GitHub analytics metrics — commits, active days, additions, deletions, net growth, churn, languages, repository activity, streaks, milestones, pull requests, and project lifecycle.
- [Developer Productivity Metrics: What to Measure and What to Avoid](https://devledger.site/blog/developer-productivity-metrics): A framework for using commits, churn, source growth, active days, repository activity, and milestones without pretending one number measures productivity.
- [What Is Code Churn? How to Read It Without Misusing It](https://devledger.site/blog/what-is-code-churn): How to calculate churn, interpret it, and avoid turning it into a misleading productivity score.
- [How to Measure Source Code Growth Over Time](https://devledger.site/blog/measure-source-code-growth-over-time): How to calculate net source growth from additions and deletions and interpret codebase growth without equating bigger with better.
- [What the GitHub Contribution Graph Doesn't Show](https://devledger.site/blog/github-contribution-graph-limitations): What the contribution graph leaves out — code growth, churn, repository lifecycles, language shifts, and context.
- [What Your Git Commit History Can Tell You About How You Work](https://devledger.site/blog/git-commit-history-analysis): How commit history reveals cadence, focus, project transitions, bursts, and gaps when treated as context rather than a score.
- [How to Compare GitHub Activity Across 7D, 30D, 90D, YTD, and 1Y](https://devledger.site/blog/compare-github-activity-time-ranges): When to use short, medium, and long windows and how to compare them without misleading yourself.
- [How to Analyze Programming Language Usage Across GitHub Repositories](https://devledger.site/blog/analyze-programming-language-usage-github): How to read language composition across repositories and distinguish snapshots from trends.
- [Repository Lifecycle Analytics: Active, Dormant, and Revived GitHub Projects](https://devledger.site/blog/repository-lifecycle-analytics): How to identify active, dormant, newly started, and revived repositories and read lifecycle patterns.
- [How to Track Developer Activity Without Storing Source Code](https://devledger.site/blog/privacy-first-github-analytics): How developer analytics can be built from repository metadata without persisting source code.
